A code block runs when the site is built, and its output is baked into the page.
Readers see the source and the result side by side -- no server, no execution in
their browser.

## A computed value

::: {#d61c160e .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 5)
np.round(np.sin(x), 4)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1}
```
array([ 0.,  1.,  0., -1., -0.])
```
:::
:::


## A chart

The same setup produces a plot. The figure below is saved as a static image at
build time.

::: {#cell-fig-sine .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.2))
ax.plot(t, np.sin(t))
ax.set_xlabel("t")
ax.set_ylabel("sin(t)")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![One period of the sine function.](index_files/figure-html/fig-sine-output-1.png){#fig-sine}
:::
:::


Because results are pre-rendered, pages stay fast and the site remains fully
static.
